title: PG Diploma in Ultrasound
description: One-year blended ultrasound program with international clinical training and an ARDMS pathway: six months of theory, three months of clinical training and a paid internship.

title: Clinical Training
description: Hands-on scanning under supervision across partner clinical locations, with regular evaluation and feedback.

title: ARDMS Preparation
description: Structured revision for the SPI and specialty examinations of the American Registry for Diagnostic Medical Sonography.

title: Paid Internship
description: Three to six months of paid clinical internship with a performance-based monthly stipend.

title: Continuing Education in Sonography
description: Short CPD modules for practising sonographers.

title: MIATA Postgraduate Sonography
description: One hour per lecturer per week while that lecturer’s module is active • 26-week programme framework
schedule_notes:
Each row represents a programme week. Dr. Niveditha’s session is on Sunday. Dr. Bagyavasan’s session is planned for a weekday. The remaining lecturer sessions can be arranged on mutually agreed days. A lecturer’s stream ends when the listed module is complete; the timetable does not extend that stream simply to fill six months.
This is a 26-week programme framework from 19 October 2026 to 18 April 2027. Week ranges are planning periods; confirm exact class dates and times with each lecturer.
Target delivery is one hour per lecturer per week while that lecturer’s module is active. This is a five-hour weekly teaching load at the start of the programme, subject to lecturer availability.
Dr. Niveditha’s classes are scheduled for Sundays, not Saturdays.
Dr. Bagyavasan’s classes are scheduled on weekdays, as requested.
Dr. Saranya’s gynaecology and breast syllabus is planned to conclude in Week 8. Dr. Suzmitha’s nerves, nerve blocks and neurosonography syllabus is planned to conclude in Week 12. Jai’s MSK syllabus is planned to conclude in Week 24. These are proposed end points and can be brought forward if learning outcomes are achieved sooner.
After a lecturer’s module is complete, that lecturer’s weekly class stops; the remaining weeks are not filled with repetitive sessions. The programme may continue through other active modules, integration, revision and final assessments.
Scheduled teaching hours are not a substitute for supervised scanning practice, clinical placement, competency sign-off or clinical experience. These should be arranged and recorded separately.
Nerve blocks and other invasive procedures must be taught within applicable professional scope, credentialling, consent, supervision and patient-safety requirements.
Cardiac ultrasound and echocardiography are excluded from this revised curriculum.
